newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama ready to join Panamerican cable project.
newsitem.headline: Panama ready to join Panamerican cable project.

text.p: Panama is poised to join a Panamerican undersea fiber optic cable project following Tuesday's partial privatization of state telephone utility INTEL, a government official said Wednesday.
Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc won a controlling 49 percent interest in INTEL with a bid of $652 million.

Panama will now be able to meet its $5.5 million funding and technological obligations to bring the Panamerican Undersea Cable System through the isthmus next year, said the official, who asked not to be identified.
"We spoke to both companies before the bid and they expressed interest in the project," he said.
GTE Corp offered $452 million for INTEL, below the government's price of $500 million. No other companies had registered to bid in the auction.
Panama signed a memorandum of understanding last year to participate in the Panamerican Undersea Cable System, a $309 million project from Chile to the U.S. Virgin Islands, he said.

Some 40 international companies from the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe and Asia are participating in the project to lay a 4,300-mile (7,000-km) undersea fiber optic cable through the Americas by September 1998, he said.
The cable will come from Chile and pass through Peru, Ecuador, Panama, Colombia, Venezuela, Aruba and the U.S. Virgin Islands, he said.
Participating companies include AT&T Corp, Sprint Corp, MCI Communications Corp, Venezuela's CANTV, Telefonica de Espana, Italy's Telecom Italia and Japan's Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co, he said.
